heroLead: Gentle 1:1 sessions of easy movement, breathwork, and rest, built around your body, your routine, and how you feel each day. Practised alongside the care your doctor provides.
empathyLabel: You don't have to do this alone
empathyText: Managing blood sugar is a daily job. Yoga can be one gentle, sustainable thing you add to your week, never something that replaces what your doctor has you doing.
helpsSubhead: Four gentle levers, working together, and the first one does most of the lifting.

levers.title: Movement uses up sugar
levers.body: When your muscles work, they draw glucose from your blood. Gentle, regular movement is the heart of every session.

levers.title: Calmer mind, steadier sugar
levers.body: Stress can nudge blood sugar upward. Breathwork and relaxation help quiet that response.

levers.title: Supports a healthy weight
levers.body: Consistent, sustainable activity supports weight management, which matters a great deal in type 2 diabetes.

levers.title: Better sleep, better days
levers.body: Poor sleep makes blood sugar harder to manage. Restful practice helps you wind down and rest more deeply.

posesH2: The poses we focus on, and why.
posesSubhead: Grouped by what they do for the body. Your teacher draws from these, and won't ask you to do all of them.

poseGroups.why: The strongest lever: working muscles use up glucose.

poses.desc: A flowing sequence, paced to you, that warms the whole body and gets you moving. A chair version is always available.
Grounding, balance, and posture work to begin exactly where your body is today.
A gentle lift that builds strength through the legs and back without strain.

poseGroups.why: Traditionally used to gently work the belly and aid digestion.

poses.desc: A gentle twist through the midsection that aids digestion and eases stiffness.

One of the few poses you can hold right after a meal to aid digestion.

poseGroups.why: Calming the stress response that can push sugar up.

poses.desc: Slow, even breathing that settles the nervous system.
A soothing, low exhale that helps unwind tension.

poseGroups.why: Good rest supports calmer, steadier days.

A still close to every session, letting everything you've done settle in.

selectionNote: Your teacher won't hand you all of these. They'll choose the right few for your body, your level, and how you're feeling that day.
howH2: How we work with you to get there.
howSubhead: One teacher who knows your name and your goals, not a different face every week.

steps.title: We get to know you
steps.body: A relaxed first session: your diagnosis, what your doctor advises, your routine, fitness, and anything to work around, such as foot sensitivity, eye or blood-pressure concerns.

steps.title: A plan shaped to you
steps.body: Your teacher chooses the poses, pace, and timing that suit you, chair options and after-meal timing included.

steps.title: Guided live 1:1s
steps.body: The same teacher every time, online, adjusting each session to how you feel and what your week has been like.

steps.title: We grow it gently
steps.body: Small, steady progress and habits you can actually keep, always alongside your medical care.

whoForText: Adults who want to support a healthy, active routine, keep moving gently, and ease everyday stress, at any level of fitness or flexibility.
testimonialQuote: I started after my type 2 diagnosis, nervous about getting it wrong. My teacher built everything around me, even what time of day to practise. A few months in, I just feel steadier, and I actually look forward to it.

faqs.q: Can yoga replace my diabetes medication?
faqs.a: No. Yoga sits alongside the care your doctor provides, and it isn't a substitute for diagnosis, treatment, or medication. Never change anything your doctor has prescribed without speaking to them first.

faqs.q: Do I need to be fit or flexible to start?
faqs.a: Not at all. Sessions begin wherever you are, with chair options and gentler variations whenever you need them. The goal is steady, comfortable movement, not touching your toes.

faqs.q: How soon might I notice anything?
faqs.a: Everyone is different. Many people first notice steadier energy, calmer stress, and better sleep. Physical changes come gradually, with consistency, which is exactly what a regular 1:1 routine is built to support.

faqs.q: Is it safe if I have neuropathy or eye concerns?
faqs.a: Tell your teacher and we'll adapt, with softer footwork, fewer inversions, and gentler pacing. Please check with your doctor too, so we can plan your sessions around their guidance.

faqs.q: When's the best time to practise?
faqs.a: After a meal rather than on an empty stomach, with a quick sugar source nearby, and not right after medication unless your teacher has planned the session around it.

safetyTitle: Yoga supports your care, it doesn't replace it
safetyText: These sessions support your overall wellbeing and are practised alongside professional medical care. They are not a substitute for diagnosis, treatment, or medication. Please tell your teacher about any conditions or symptoms so they can adapt your session safely, and keep your doctor in the loop.
metaDescription: Gentle 1:1 yoga for diabetes: easy movement, breathwork, and rest that may support steady energy, a healthy weight, and calmer everyday stress, practised alongside your medical care. First session free.
